preamble: Diphthongization of [ɛ] to a front-closing diphthong adds a high front off-glide, here written with the atlas symbol ei. Quebec French breaks long /ɛː/ into [ɛɪ̯] in open syllables (fête, pêcher), and most Brazilian Portuguese speakers insert a [j] glide after a stressed final vowel before a coda sibilant, so dez 'ten' is [dɛjs] and pés 'feet' [ˈpɛ(ɪ̯)s], while European Portuguese keeps /ˈdɛʃ/.

examples.note: Long /ɛː/ is diphthongized to [ɛɪ̯] in open syllables, but not before /ʁ/ (mairie [mɛːʁi]). [ɛɪ̯] = atlas ei.

languageExamples.context: Stressed word-final vowel before a coda sibilant

examples.note: Most Brazilian speakers diphthongize stressed vowels in oxytones before a sibilant coda; [ɛɪ̯] = atlas ei.
